title: From Local Skills to Long-Horizon Tasks: Progressive Skill Exploration for LLM Web Agents
claim: Complex long-horizon exploration succeeds by iteratively discovering, composing, and expanding local skills, using failures to guide new exploration.
layout: Top loop banner plus 3 detail panels below; left-to-right flow with cyclic return arrow
description: A large top panel, 'Progressive Exploration', shows a trajectory of blue observation circles (O) and green action circles (A) joined by arrows and squiggly connectors, ending in an orange reward node (R). Dashed green boxes above the trajectory name Skill 1–3. Dashed magenta boxes below it name failures such as a pagination loop and a hallucinated response. A left legend explains skill memory and failure memory. A cyclic row of Skill Discovery, Orchestrate and Expansion modules loops back to 'Start a New Rollout'. Three detail panels sit below. Skill Discovery (blue border) turns raw trajectories into skill and failure summaries. Skill Orchestrate (green border) selects states by novelty and builds a skill graph. Skill Expansion (purple border) shows robust skill chain execution and teacher and self interventions. Colors code skills, failures and states.
caption: Overview of SCOPE’s progressive exploration framework: Skill Discovery extracts local skills and failure experiences from historical trajectories; Skill Orchestration composes local skills into skill chains; and Skill Expansion uses chain-aligned failure experiences to guide exploration.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are driving autonomous agents toward real-world environments, with the Web emerging as one of the most representative interaction scenarios. However, training Web agents with naive exploration remains challenging: successful trajectories are rare, and the sparse terminal rewards make it difficult for agents to obtain useful feedback from failed trajectories. Inspired by skill acquisition theory, we propose Skill-Composed Progressive Exploration (SCOPE), a short-to-long learning framework for long-horizon Web agents that decomposes complex task exploration into a gradual expansion process from local skills to complete task-solving capability. Specifically, SCOPE iteratively explores around local skills: Skill Discovery extracts reusable local skills and failure experiences from historical rollouts; Skill Orchestration composes discovered skills into high-level skill chains; and Skill Expansion leverages failure experiences aligned with the current skill chain to guide the agent toward exploring new subskills. Through this process, SCOPE progressively constructs task-completing skill chains across rollouts and internalizes them into the policy parameters through agentic on-policy distillation. Extensive experiments on WebArena, WebVoyager, and WebShop show that SCOPE consistently improves exploration dynamics and achieves 3.9% to 18.6% relative gains over the strongest baselines in each setting.
